assetRisk.scenario: Statutory customs and excise inventory audit penalty or duty remission disallowance
assetRisk.source: ~10-11 refineries processing ~80 MMTPA (~1.6 Mbbl/d). Under national customs bonded warehousing regulations (Customs Act Chapter IX, Sec 72) and central excise rules governing petroleum manufacturing losses and duty-exempt internal fuel consumption, refineries must account for raw crude inputs and maintain auditable mass balances within statutory tolerance limits (typically <=0.5% to 1.0%). Frequency (0.20) reflects one major statutory excise/customs inventory audit dispute, show-cause notice (SCN), or shortage challenge per refinery every 5 years (~2.2 events/year across the estate). Consequence (₹16 Cr / ~US$1.9M) reflects differential excise/customs duty demands on unexplained material balance deficits (e.g., 0.2-0.3% unexplained loss on an average 7.5 MMTPA refinery = 15,000-22,500 MT, taxed at ₹15,000-₹20,000/MT), statutory interest under Sec 28AA/11AA, and adjudicated penalties under Sec 114A/11AC or appellate true-up settlements. Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to information defects (unreconciled book-to-physical inventory lags, unverified flare/evaporative loss documentation per Energy Institute HM 31, and missing fuel gas mass totalizer logs); beta (0.40) reflects the 7-agent squad's efficacy in maintaining continuous automated mass balance closure, gross error detection, and certified excise audit packages.

rationale: P48 Hydrocarbon Accountant serves as the physical and fiscal custodian of refinery and pipeline material balances across 11 refineries (~80 MMTPA throughput), ~20,000 km of pipelines, and ~120 marketing installations. Sizing at 80 seats is defensibly distributed: ~50 technical accountants across 11 refineries (averaging 4-5 per refinery covering daily unit mass balances, tank inventory closures, and excise records), ~13 across regional pipeline operating divisions (custody batch tickets, prover audits, and transmix interface reconciliation), ~11 across major marketing distribution terminals (terminal stock balances and transit loss monitoring), and ~6 at corporate headquarters (marine charter-party demurrage audits and enterprise loss control governance), representing ~0.26% of enterprise headcount. Asset Capital is strictly null in accordance with value_model.js rules: hydrocarbon accounting workflows are retrospective analytical reconciliations (06:00-09:00 AM daily closing and month-end) that do not sit on the critical path of physical process units or flowing pipelines; claiming volume-based giveaway or yield recovery would double-count P16 (Refined Product Yield), P28 (Product Blending Quality), and P15/P29 (Demurrage). Asset Risk captures avoided statutory customs and excise penalties and duty remission disallowances on unexplained inventory deficits and fuel gas consumption across 11 refineries (frequency 0.20/yr, consequence ₹16 Cr, alpha 0.35, beta 0.40, yielding ₹4.93 Cr/yr in avoided expected losses with alpha*beta held to 0.14). Resource Recovery is strictly null as the persona operates downstream of production and does not influence subsurface reservoir recovery, satisfying the portfolio rule prohibiting joint Integrity and Recovery claims.
caveats: 1. Asset capital is maintained as null to protect the model's 'load-bearing zero' discipline; if an operator insists on capturing commercial transit loss recoveries on imported marine crude (~500 Mbbl/yr marine crude imports with 0.02% recovered shortage claims per API MPMS Chapter 17 at ₹300/bbl margin), that volume mechanism would generate ~₹3.0 Cr/yr, but represents a commercial counter-claim against shipowners rather than physical asset critical-path efficiency. 2. Failure consequence assumes large integrated refining complexes where excise duty on petroleum fuels remains outside the GST framework, retaining steep Central Excise exposure (₹13-₹20/liter on transportation fuels) and Customs bonded warehouse liabilities. 3. Alpha and beta strictly reflect informational decision support; final commercial dispute sign-offs and legal tax return submissions remain with corporate finance and legal leadership.
